limitations: Synthetic measurements and equipment parameters
Reduced lumped thermal dynamics; no native vessel/pipeline transient qualification
Fixed composition, cooler temperatures and assumed off-design efficiency curves
Optimization is a local candidate inside the sampled domain
Empirical residual threshold is not a guaranteed probability bound
Network scaling timings compare different workloads, not simulator speedup
Official equinor/timeseriesanalysis-py wrapper repository and README returned 404; its API and execution are not validated
TSA 1.4.38 needs explicit steady PID output seeds for this multi-input graph; subsequent values are proven to come from simulation
Common utility is a prescribed lag, without load-to-utility feedback or a water energy balance
12 K utility stress can extrapolate beyond the identification domain; it is a numerical limit/recovery test
New stabilization case is inspired by comparesimulations2; no reproduction of its petroleum assay or benchmark results
JSON route choices are engineered alternatives, not arbitrary topology synthesis or proof of global optimality
Stable-oil and export-gas product-quality constraints, compressor maps, hydraulics and economics are outside this example
JSON alone does not determine TSA time constants; local projection uses explicitly assumed 10-90 s response times
Material recycle is solved in NeqSim; TSA receives full-process local sensitivities without duplicating material edges
Full-process identification is validated on synthetic low-noise data, not field measurements
Six learned KPI responses summarize a 24-unit physical process; no unit-by-unit dynamic inventory or hydraulic equivalence is claimed
Generator lags and pressure-actuator response are explicit assumptions requiring field qualification
Nominal 2% driver backoff is an engineering allowance, not a quantified uncertainty guarantee
Local saving is relative to 37/9 bara and must not be added to the earlier baseline-to-optimum saving
